title: Customer edge ask stitchbook — compact synthesis
content:
Purpose and framing:
This doc is a compact, action-oriented stitchbook of small-but-high-frequency customer asks that don’t neatly belong in our large feature backlog. Goal: give eng + product a prioritized set of low-effort remediations, concrete workarounds, and middling-impact feature sketches that reduce friction for customers using Redwood Hosted and Dedicated in production.

Methodology (how this was built):
- Source signals: support transcripts (last 6 months), CSM call notes, two post-onboarding surveys, Slack escalations, and telemetry spikes (error/latency tags).
- Inclusion criteria: repeated ask (>=3 unique customers), clear user-experience pain or operational burden, and plausible remediation path (workaround, doc, or small product change).
- Quick impact scoring: frequency x customer-severity (1–5 each). Effort rough-class: tiny (docs/playbook), small (product toggle/config), medium (API change), larger (backend routing).

Synthesis — recurring micro-themes (ranked by frequency * severity):
1) Token billing confusion on retries (impact score: 16).
   - Problem: customers see unexpected token charges when client libraries retry a generation after partial streaming. Many assume retries are free or deduplicated by the server.
   - Representative note: "We retried twice when the websocket dropped and our monthly bill doubled—totally surprised."
   - Short-term patch: docs + SDK snippet showing idempotency keys for streaming endpoints; server-side guidance doc for handling partials. (Effort: tiny)
   - Medium-term product gap: server-side idempotent retry primitive that avoids charging the same request twice when the client signals a retry within a short window. (Effort: medium)

2) Latency tail for mixed-priority workloads (impact score: 14).
   - Problem: customers with both interactive low-latency routes and batch tasks see tail latency spikes during short bursts; current routing blends them and degrades the interactive path.
   - Workaround used by customers: run separate api keys and run batch jobs in off-peak times or on Dedicated. Pain: not every customer can procure Dedicated immediately.
   - Quick fix: routing guidance + recommended autoscaling configs for common burst patterns; example config templates. (Effort: tiny)
   - Product idea: light-weight per-key routing priority layer (priority hints in request header) to avoid tail impact. (Effort: medium)

3) Confusing model-variant fallbacks and quality regressions (impact score: 12).
   - Problem: automatic fallbacks to quantized or smaller variants sometimes change output characteristics unexpectedly for customers. They want predictable fallbacks or opt-out.
   - Customer quote: "Our prompts were tuned to the base model; fallback changed tone and broke a pipeline."
   - Short-term: add a doc section "Model Variant Behavior & Best Practices" and provide an explicit prompt-compatibility checklist. (Effort: tiny)
   - Mid-term: expose per-deployment fallback controls in Console (opt-out, strict-match, or similarity threshold). (Effort: medium)

4) Embeddings drift during model upgrades (impact score: 10).
   - Problem: customers using embeddings for production retrieval notice semantic drift after model upgrades; no clear mechanism for comparing old vs new embeddings before rollout.
   - Short-term remediation: provide a small eval harness template + scripts (in repo) to compute pairwise drift and recommended thresholds. (Effort: tiny)
   - Feature ask: Console comparison view: sample recall/precision delta pre-rollout with toggle to pin old embedding model. (Effort: medium)

5) Poor error transparency for Private deployments (impact score: 9).
   - Problem: logs in Private/VPC are noisy and not mapped to helpful remediation steps. Customers often escalate to SRE for things that could be self-diagnosed.
   - Quick win: curated runbook snippets for the top 7 Private errors, with diagnostic CLI commands. (Effort: tiny)

Representative short vignettes (anonymized):
- Customer: FinRiskCo (midmarket) — use case: automated doc summarization. Pain: bursts during month-end cause retries and double-billing; workaround: move heavy summarization to nightly cron, but business needs same-day.
- Customer: ChatRetailer (scale startup) — use case: chat assistant with product tool-calls. Pain: model fallback changed slot-filling behavior. They requested an explicit per-route fallback opt-out.
- Customer: DataIndexer (B2B search infra) — use case: embeddings-based ranking. Pain: minor recall drop after a managed model upgrade; requested an A/B-style rollout for embedding models.

Concrete short-term remediation catalog (first 8 weeks):
- Docs + SDK snippets: idempotency for streaming and retries (owner: devx), routing config templates (owner: infra-books), model-variant guidance (owner: product-hosted-api).
- Small Console tweaks (2-sprint scope): explanatory tooltip for fallback behavior, add "pin model" flag for embeddings (owner: product-console).
- Runbooks: top-7 Private errors (owner: security-and-compliance ops lead), distribute to customer onboarding playbook.

Mid-term product sketches (quarter horizon):
- Request header hinting for priority routing: allow clients to mark request importance with budgeted fallbacks. Use-case: interactive vs batch isolation. Value: reduces tail latency for critical routes.
- Embedding-model rollout comparator: sample-based drift visualization + suggested roll criteria.
- Server-side short-window idempotency: de-duplicate retried streamed generations within X seconds when client-supplied idempotency token exists.

Estimated impact vs effort (rough):
- Docs & SDK snippets: high impact, low effort. (PRIORITY: immediate)
- Runbooks for Private errors: medium impact, low effort. (PRIORITY: immediate)
- Console tooltip + pin flag for embeddings: medium impact, small effort. (PRIORITY: near-term)
- Priority routing header + server changes: high impact, medium-to-high effort. (PRIORITY: Q2 initiative)

Unresolved questions / trade-offs:
- Billing dedupe window: what is acceptable default for idempotent retry deduplication (5s, 30s, 120s)? Larger windows risk hiding legitimately new requests. Need billing/legal input.
- Priority routing fairness: do we expose priority hints to all customers or only Dedicated tiers? Risk of abuse if unlimited.
- Embedding pinning lifecycle: how do we surface guidance to encourage customers to re-evaluate pins periodically?

Immediate next steps (owners & deadlines):
- Create doc PR: "Handling retries & streaming idempotency" — assignee: Diego Marquez — due: 2024-12-01.
- Add routing templates to repo: infra-books — assignee: Samir Gupta — due: 2024-12-08.
- Build minimal eval harness for embeddings drift (repo + example): assignee: Ruth Kim — due: 2024-12-15.
- Internal sync: short 30-minute design review for server-side idempotency and priority routing — invite: infra, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api — date: 2024-12-04.

Notes to self / open invites:
- This is intentionally compact — the aim is to reduce ops noise and unblock customers quickly. If product wants a separate, larger PRD for the routing work, I can expand.
- Please paste additional customer quotes or ticket ids below; will fold into the next iteration.

Appendix: quick FAQ for CSMs to surface to customers:
Q: Why did my retry cost tokens?
A: Current behavior charges each unique request; we recommend client-side idempotency tokens and SDK best-practices. See linked SDK snippet.

Q: Can I prevent fallbacks that change model tone?
A: You can pin model variants in Dedicated or request a strict-fallback policy via support for Hosted; Console opt-out will be available soon.

Owners / contact for follow-ups: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.example), Diego Marquez, Ruth Kim.

--- end stitchbook entry ---
